summary: H.R. 6501, titled the 'Bipartisan Health Insurance Affordability Act', extends and modifies enhanced premium tax credits for health insurance under the Internal Revenue Code and the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act through 2027. It establishes new guardrails to prevent fraud in health insurance exchanges by setting civil and criminal penalties for agents and brokers, adds requirements for agent-assisted enrollments and deceased individual removals, adjusts the annual open enrollment period for 2026, regulates pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) regarding transparency, reporting, and 100 percent rebate pass-throughs, and allows certain qualified exchange enrollees to establish and fund Health Savings Accounts (HSAs).

affected_groups.effect: Receive extended and modified enhanced premium tax credits, optional prepayment of annual premiums, options to direct partial advance payments of premium tax credits into HSAs, and eligibility to establish HSAs under certain exchange plans.

Subject to stricter verification processes for enrollments, increased oversight, audits, lists of suspended or terminated brokers, standard of proof rules, and potential civil or criminal penalties for negligence or fraudulent information.

Subject to new transparency rules, strict limitations on remuneration (limiting income to bona fide service fees), mandatory 100 percent rebate pass-throughs, annual reporting mandates, and audit requirements.
affected_groups.group: Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBMs) and Plan Sponsors

key_provisions: Extends and modifies enhanced premium tax credits through taxable years beginning before January 1, 2028, setting specific premium assistance amounts and sliding scales for different household income percentages relative to the poverty line.

Establishes civil and criminal penalties for agents and brokers who provide false or fraudulent information or exhibit negligence during exchange enrollments, and requires verification processes for agent-assisted enrollments.
Requires the Secretary to check the Death Master File quarterly to remove deceased individuals from exchange qualified health plans.
Extends the annual open enrollment period for the 2026 plan year to run from November 1, 2025, to March 1, 2026.
Imposes new PBM transparency, reporting, and 100 percent rebate pass-through requirements for Medicare Part D prescription drug plans and group health plans starting in 2029.

Allows qualified Exchange enrollees who purchase the lowest-cost bronze plan or a plan with a lower monthly premium than the previous year to establish and contribute to Health Savings Accounts (HSAs).

summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 6501, titled the 'Bipartisan Health Insurance Affordability Act', extends and modifies enhanced premium tax credits for health insurance under the Internal Revenue Code and the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act through 2027. It establishes new guardrails to prevent fraud in health insurance exchanges by setting civil and criminal penalties for agents and brokers, adds requirements for agent-assisted enrollments and deceased individual removals, adjusts the annual open enrollment period for 2026, regulates pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) regarding transparency, reporting, and 100 percent rebate pass-throughs, and allows certain qualified exchange enrollees to establish and fund Health Savings Accounts (HSAs).
summary_detail.significance: The legislation directly alters federal health insurance subsidies, exchange operations, agent regulations, and prescription drug benefit management rules. It involves significant funding provisions, including $113 million for CMS program management, $20 million for the HHS Inspector General, and $1 million for the Medicare Payment Advisory Commission for fiscal year 2026.
